newsitem.title: INDIA: Arafat to attend non-aligned meeting in India.
newsitem.headline: Arafat to attend non-aligned meeting in India.

text.p: Palestinian President Yasser Arafat will arrive in New Delhi on Sunday for a one-day visit to address a meeting of the Non-Aligned Movement (NAM) and confer with Indian leaders, Palestinian officials said. Arafat was expected to arrive in the Indian capital late on Sunday and address a special plenary session of the meeting of foreign ministers of NAM on Monday morning, the ambassador to India Khalid el-Sheikh told Reuters.
The Palestinians hold the vice presidency of the 113-member NAM.
Arafat was to meet President Shankar Dayal Sharma, Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda and Foreign Minister Inder Kumar Gujral on Monday.

The Palestinian ambassador to India said senior officials of NAM member states on Saturday approved a draft resolution expressing support for the Palestinian people and criticising Israeli policies towards Jerusalem and settlements.

The resolution, which will be considered by NAM foreign ministers during their two-day meeting beginning on Monday, calls for a special session of the United Nations General Assembly on the Palestinian issue, he said.

The Indian Foreign Ministry said India and the Palestinians enjoyed friendly relations, and New Delhi had extended unfailing support for the Palestinian people, the Press Trust of India said, quoting a ministry statement.
The ministry said India also supported the Middle East peace process and had expressed deep concern over recent developments, the news agency said.

Israel's ground breaking of a new Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem last month triggered daily Palestinian clashes with Israeli troops, halted peace talks and angered the rest of the Arab world.

On Saturday, Palestinian officials warned of a "comprehensive explosion" in the peace process which could lead to more confrontations and said they were sending a message to U.S. President Bill Clinton.
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu was scheduled to meet Clinton on Monday.
